items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: ai-raccoon model set local (bundled ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2, activated before writing) ; wrote 4 entries (sextant target + JWT/auth, password-reset, decision distractors) ; confirmed embed_state=embedded (1536-byte/384-dim blobs) via ?mode=ro before searching ; memory_search default weights, query='an old-fashioned tool sailors used to gauge their position by watching the stars from the deck at night' (zero literal overlap with the sextant text) ; same query with ftsWeight=0/vectorWeight=1 and with ftsWeight=1/vectorWeight=0 to isolate each leg ; memory_search query='reset your password account settings security' (literal-overlap control)
items.evidence:
Default hybrid (1:1) -> ranked: JWT/auth (1.0), sextant (0.984), password-reset (0.968), decision (0.953) -- sextant present at rank 2, not rank 1.
Vector-only (ftsWeight=0) -> sextant (1.0) rank 1, JWT (0.984), decision (0.968), password-reset (0.953) -- confirms the semantic leg alone puts the target first.
FTS-only (vectorWeight=0) -> JWT (1.0) rank 1, password-reset (0.984), sextant (0.968), decision (0.953) -- FTS5's documented OR-fallback (no AND match, so it falls back to an OR of every content token) matches every doc on some stray token and produces this near-arbitrary order in a 4-doc corpus.
Literal-overlap control -> password-reset ranks 1 (1.0), reordering correctly vs. the semantic query.
items.observed-result: The entry IS returned through hybrid search (rank 2 of 4, well inside default minRelativeScore=0), and isolating the two legs proves both are functioning: the vector leg alone puts the zero-overlap target at rank 1, and the FTS leg alone (via the documented OR-fallback for an under-matching query) is what pulls the unrelated JWT entry ahead of it under default 1:1 weights in this small corpus. The literal-overlap control confirms ranking is query-sensitive, not fixed.
items.acceptance-reason: The item's contract (memory_search retrieves the entry through hybrid RRF) is met and verified live; the counter-intuitive rank-2 result under default weights is explained and reproduced deliberately by isolating each leg, not hand-waved -- it is FTS5's documented OR-fallback behavior in a small corpus, not a broken vector leg.

items.expected-result: `ai-raccoon model set code default` against a scratch data root with no prior download resolves and downloads `faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1` into `<data-root>/models/faxenoff__code-daemon-embed-v1`, then activates it — writing embedding.codeModel/codeEngine — with NO manifest hand-edit (#422's done-criterion). Re-running the same command against an already-downloaded directory only re-activates, with no re-fetch. After activation, the code-reindex job drains any pending code rows to 0. The ~187 MB download may be substituted against a pre-downloaded model directory if network egress is infeasible in this run; record as `substituted` naming the pre-downloaded path used.
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch>/root --port 55014 model set code default (fresh scratch root, no prior download) ; sqlite3 ?mode=ro settings/code_entries ; repeated on a SECOND independent scratch root+server with a .ts fixture ; waited 60s+ polling code_entries.embed_state after each
items.evidence:
Download+activate output (both roots) -> 'downloaded faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1@main to <dir> (4 file(s)); ai-raccoon.manifest.json written. ... code embedding engine set to local (<dir>); the code-reindex maintenance job will re-embed pending rows.' No --yes needed (187 MB < 500 MB threshold), no manifest hand-edit performed by me. settings.embedding.codeModel/codeEngine written; manifest dims=768, contextWindowTokens=512 (matches the #453 fix, not the old 128). shasum of downloaded model.onnx/sentencepiece.bpe.model matched the manifest's own sha256 pins exactly (no corruption).
BUT: code_entries.embed_state stayed 'pending' on BOTH roots after 60s+ of live polling; the code-reindex maintenance job DID run repeatedly (server log: 'code-reindex ... ran in 859 ms' then '27 ms' then '14 ms', then stopped polling it — HasWorkAsync went false). code_entries.embed_attempts reached 3 (=CodeCorpusSchema.MaxEmbedAttempts, the literal cap in src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Sqlite/MemorySql.cs), so the row is now permanently excluded from selection — a poison row, stuck pending forever, not a transient delay.
items.observed-result: The download+activate half of #422's one-command install works exactly as designed: real download, real sha256-pinned files, real settings write, no manifest hand-edit. But the drain half FAILS: the code-reindex job silently exhausts MaxEmbedAttempts=3 on the very first, smallest possible fixture (a 2-function Python file, then independently a 2-function TypeScript file) without ever marking a single row embedded, and never logs a warning/error — the failure is only visible via the code_entries.embed_attempts column or by then running a kind=code search (see 'code-search-discriminates-on-engine-activation' below, which surfaces the underlying exception text).
items.acceptance-reason: REGRESSION, reproduced twice independently (two scratch roots, two servers, two unrelated file types/languages). The one-command install's stated contract — 'downloads and activates it... after activation, the code-reindex job drains any pending code rows to 0' — is NOT met: the row never drains, it silently poisons out after 3 attempts. This is the actual, functional end of #422/#453's own promise (a working default code search), not just the CLI ergonomics half, so it is not accepted. Flagged to the owner as a STOP-and-report regression, not fixed here — see the coordinator report.
